arguments.task: Audit a TYPO3 extension that ships one content element with PrismJS assets, a CKEditor integration, a site set and an event listener
Composer extension package identity, ext_emconf metadata, autoloading and supported TYPO3 version range
Fluid template escaping, raw output of user-supplied code, and secure rendering in frontend content element templates
CKEditor RTE integration and frontend JavaScript and CSS assets shipped by an extension

outcomes.evidence: `typo3_project_scope` and `typo3_extension_scope` are the first two server calls of the session, ahead of the task guide, and what they returned is what the answer argues from. The declared range is the measure throughout: the context line reads "the package declares `^13.4 || ^14.3` on PHP `>=8.2`" against an installation of 14.3.0, and finding 5 kills a `getMajorVersion() >= 13` branch as unconditionally true given that range. The repository-owned commands are not merely named this time — `composer test:php:lint` and `composer cgl:ci` were executed and their output is in the context line ("OK, 122 files", "no violations"), and finding 1 traces `composer test` through `@test:php:lint` to the same linter. Two facts are operative rather than stated in their own right: the extension key appears only as `EXT:syntax/...`, `tt_content.syntax` and the `syntax/base` set, and the standalone-versus-installation distinction only as the core read out of `.build/vendor/typo3/cms-core` while every consequence is argued for "every site depending on `syntax/base`" rather than for this one.

Every finding carries a path and most a line, and nine claims were re-checked against the checkout while judging. All nine hold: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a 2×4 matrix whose only steps are `composer test:php:lint` and `composer cgl:ci`; there is no `Tests/` directory; `partialRootPaths.1` and `layoutRootPaths.1` point at two directories that do not exist; `Configuration/Sets/Base/` holds `config.yaml`, `settings.definitions.yaml` and `setup.typoscript` and no `labels.xlf`; `typo3/cms-t3editor` is absent from `.build/vendor/typo3/`; the `E_USER_DEPRECATED` for an `ext_emconf.php` is at `PackageManager.php:936-943` and `isComposerOnlyCapable()` at 954 requires both `providesPackages` and a version; `RteConfigEnhancer` appends `codeBlock` and overwrites `$configuration['codeBlock']` with twenty languages under no condition at all; `CodeEditorFormatDataProvider` lists eight formats including `sql` and carries the `@todo`; and `CHANGELOG.md` 1.1.0 records the conditional loader added in 82d1545, which 85c8d3f deleted and cc85356 replaced with the set. What is new against the three earlier runs is the third kind of evidence: two findings rest on a command that was run rather than on the file that declares it. Two imprecisions, neither of which moves a finding: the assets are called unconditional where two of the seven includes are gated on `{$plugin.tx_syntax.settings.plugins.linenumbers}` by `if.isTrue`, and `ci.yml` has a second job — a node build with a `git status` clean check — that "the only steps are" passes over. Only surfaces the extension has are opened, and `typo3_extension_scope` reporting `tests: []` and `manual: null` is what two findings are built on.

All six areas appear and each is anchored. Compatibility: the `ext_emconf.php` deprecation on every manifest read, and two dead version branches. Behavioral correctness: Prism CSS and JavaScript on every page of every site taking the set, an RTE listener rewriting every preset in the installation, and four hand-maintained language lists that have already drifted. Test evidence: finding 1, that a matrix whose two axes produce identical work proves nothing about 13-versus-14. Documentation: no manual, a two-line README, a set with no `labels.xlf`. Release: the TER-versus-Composer metadata constraint in finding 4 and the `publish.yml` PHP 7.4 pin argued as a latent risk. Static quality is the one that changed shape: this is the first recorded run in which the checks were executed rather than read out of CI, and finding 1 makes their passing its argument — "both of which I ran and both of which pass, which is exactly the problem". What is still not named, for the second run in this checkout, is what the repository does not have: there is no PHPStan, no analysis step, no baseline, and the answer's ceiling for the existing net is "the PHP parses plus the formatting is right" without the missing analyser becoming a finding. b0eded4 gave the receiving skill that branch; the conformance checklist's quality surface still reads "tests, declared validation commands, documentation, deprecations", which asks what is declared and not what a complete check surface covers.

The order is argued rather than labelled. Finding 1 leads because the absent suite is what leaves the rest unobserved — "a core minor that changes any of those surfaces first surfaces as a user report" — and the closing line reorders the fixes against their dependencies rather than against their severities: #4 before #1 because a functional suite with `failOnDeprecation` fails on the manifest before its first assertion, #1 before #2 and #3 because the suite is what makes those safe to change. Uncertainty sits inside the finding it belongs to: the data provider's array access is sound because `typo3_configuration_lookup` shows `TcaSelectItems` running transitively before it, "though that ordering is inherited, not declared"; the Fluid layout "renders correctly, but on an undeclared dependency"; finding 6 is "defensible while 13 is supported — but nothing in the repository says that is why"; and one checked subject is reported as deliberately not a finding, the `publish.yml` PHP 7.4 pin, because `typo3/tailor` still declares `^7.2 || ^8.0`. The sentence the three earlier runs were all missing is now the first line of the answer: "No files were changed; I ran only the two commands `typo3_project_scope` marks as **check**."

Finding 1 goes to **typo3-extension-testing** with its first step bounded to functional coverage of the TCA type and the data provider, finding 2 to **typo3-content-element-development**, finding 8 to **typo3-extension-documentation**, and the answer ends by offering an order and starting none of it. Nothing was implemented: 31 tool calls — 12 Bash, 3 Read, 2 ToolSearch, 1 Skill, 13 server calls — and not one Write, Edit or NotebookEdit, with `git status` in the checkout afterwards showing only the ` M .gitignore` and `?? .mcp.json` the install left. The two commands it did run are the two the scope marks as checks. The routing is thinner than the previous run's, which carried a workflow on every finding: four of the eight carry one here, and findings 3, 5, 6 and 7 — all of them content-element and registration work — are left without a named owner.

failures.evidence: The coverage table closes surfaces the extension does not have rather than asking for them. Persistence is clean with a reason — `syntax_language varchar(60)` is "a genuine delta TCA cannot derive", no DataHandler use, no upgrade wizard needed, `l10n_mode => exclude` right for a language selector. Security is clean by inspection rather than by checklist: Fluid escaping by default, no `f:format.raw`, a fixed-item select, the `defined('TYPO3')` guards, the TER token read from secrets behind a repository-name gate. `.html` rather than `.fluid.html` is named as "the accepted predecessor form on 14, not a defect". No backend module, route or middleware is asked of an extension that registers none.

Compatibility is measured against the declaration and never against the installed 14.3.0. Finding 5 uses the declared `^13.4 || ^14.3` to prove a runtime branch dead rather than reading the installed major as the truth, and kills the `isLoaded('t3editor')` branch by establishing that the package exists on neither supported major. Finding 6 argues *for* the older major — shipping settings twice "is defensible while 13 is supported" — and finding 1's whole case is that the matrix which exists to prove the declared range never exercises it. Where the installed core is read it is read for a mechanism: `PackageManager::getComposerManifest()` and `isComposerOnlyCapable()`, and `ExtensionManagementUtility::addRecordType()` as the v13+ convention.

Nothing from the core contribution process appears: no `runTests.sh`, no `Build/Scripts`, no Gerrit. Every command named or executed is this repository's own — `composer test:php:lint`, `composer cgl:ci`, `composer test`, and `composer show typo3/tailor` to settle the pin — and the CI finding is precisely that this project's own matrix does not exercise this project's own declared range. Where a convention comes from outside it is the core's or the extension's own history: `addRecordType()` from the installed `ExtensionManagementUtility`, the conditional loader from this repository's own CHANGELOG and git log.

No file was changed and no tool that could change one was called; the two commands that ran are the two the scope marks as handing the code back as it was, and the answer says so before its first finding. Recommendations stay recommendations: the Tailor pin "works today", finding 5's `addTcaSelectItem` is "convention drift" rather than a break with `addRecordType` verified as present and not deprecated, finding 6 is "defensible", finding 7's tag-versus-attribute registration is named as convention. The verdict that leans furthest past its evidence is finding 2's "Every page of every site depending on `syntax/base` ships them": the chain through `setup.typoscript` is complete and re-checked, but the behaviour was reasoned about rather than rendered, and two of the seven includes are in fact gated on a setting.

notes:
The fourth recorded REVIEW-02 run, the second in /home/benji/projects/syntax, and the first against a server that tells a review to run the checks it cannot break anything with. Session b5df3449-084c-4ae6-a2d2-90dd3b47381c, 2026-07-31 13:32-13:37 CEST, five minutes, one prompt and no steering. The run it replaces is in commit 3390f34, judged `covered` against the same criteria digest at 12:21 the same day.

Setup. /home/benji/projects/syntax at dc94545, `bk2k/syntax` 5.0.0, TYPO3 14.3.0 below `.build/vendor`, declared range `^13.4 || ^14.3`, DDEV up. The server is not a Composer dependency there, so the skills were republished from this checkout with `install --agent=claude` immediately before the run and `references/base.md` verified byte-identical to `skills/base.md`. 428 tests green.

What this run was for. It re-ran the query of the open note — no extension review has reached the console half of this server — against the server as it is now, and the note is answered by it. Three earlier runs called no installation-backed tool at all, with DDEV up and reachable each time. This one called two: `typo3_configuration_lookup` on `SYS/formEngine/formDataGroup/tcaDatabaseRecord`, answered by the installation's own console through DDEV with the real form data group, and `typo3_icon_lookup` on `content-element-syntax`, an exact match resolved from `EXT:syntax/Configuration/Icons.php`. Neither is decorative: the first settles that `TcaSelectItems` runs transitively before the extension's data provider, which is what makes `['syntax_language'][0]` correct, and the second closes the Icons row of the coverage table. So a review of a reusable extension does reach the installation, and the console half is no longer exercised only in E-SITE. What it did not ask is `typo3_label_lookup` on the Labels surface it assessed from the XLF file directly, and `typo3_documentation_lookup` was not called at all.

The other thing it settles is D-EVI-3, whose **Wrong if** was that reviews which now run the checks would report the same findings they used to read out of CI files. They did not: the two checks passing is what finding 1 is built on — a green net that is green whether or not the extension works — and the answer opens by saying which of the three kinds of evidence it stands on. That sentence was missing from all three earlier runs.

What is still missing is on the other side of the same subject. For the second run in this checkout the absence of static analysis is not a finding: no PHPStan, no analysis step, no baseline, and the review reports the ceiling of what exists rather than the layer that is not there. b0eded4 fixed the skill that would receive the work; what is left is the conformance checklist's quality surface, which names "declared validation commands" and so can only assess what the repository already declares.

Judging notes for whoever reads this next. Nine of the answer's claims were re-checked against the checkout and the installed core and all nine hold. Two imprecisions are recorded above and neither moves a finding. One thing about the server rather than the run: `typo3_project_scope` reports three of the five syntax commands as checks — `cgl:ci`, `test:php:lint`, and `test`, which resolves to `@test:php:lint` — where the message of 2bfd837 says two.
